bullets.title: July CPI Wednesday is the key macro catalyst; market pricing 52% chance of September rate hike
bullets.body: Goldman expects core CPI +0.19% m/m (below +0.2% consensus) and headline +0.05% vs +0.1% consensus. JPM's Feroli models core +0.22% (2.5% YoY). A hawkish print would have larger equity impact than bonds; options pricing ~0.9% SPX move. Fed's Hammack explicitly said current rates are 'not meaningfully restricting the economy' and she 'would probably need some number of rate hikes.'

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury yields hit 19-year high (5.28%); global sovereign yields surging
bullets.body: 30-year UST reached 5.28%, a 19-year high. France's 30-year bond yield hit its highest since the Global Financial Crisis. The 10-year yield rose to 4.70% during Monday's session. UBS mortgage finance notes Treasury curve has bear-steepened ~30 bps on the long end since quarter-end; MOVE index has declined but TLT hit its lowest closing price in over 22 years.

bullets.title: Nasdaq futures positioning turned net short for first time since May 2025—potential squeeze setup
bullets.body: Non-dealer Nasdaq futures positioning flipped net short for the first time since May 2025 as investors sold $21.6B despite a 7.1% rally. Asset managers cut NDX longs last week at -2.1 standard deviations. IWM implied vol sits at 1-year lows (16.9) with term structure in the 99th percentile. Put option costs fell to their cheapest level since April 2025, suggesting complacency.

bullets.title: S&P 500 at all-time highs, but P/B ratio surpasses dot-com bubble peak; earnings forecasts surge to 32% YoY
bullets.body: S&P 500 price-to-book ratio exceeded dot-com bubble levels. 2Q26 aggregate earnings beat estimates by 7.3% with 77% of companies beating; EPS growth now expected at 33.2% YoY for 2026. JPMorgan raised S&P 500 target to 8,000; Evercore sees 9,000 possible; BTIG warns of failed breakout risk. Mag7 group trades >2 standard deviations below mean on forward P/E, implying 30-56% upside to historical valuation.

bullets.title: Oil surges 5% on Strait of Hormuz disruption; diesel tightens on Jazan and Zawiya outages
bullets.body: WTI settled at $82.13 (+5.05%) and Brent at $87.72 (+4.99%) as US-Iran deal hopes faded; Trump said the strait is 'a little complex because of occasional mines.' Saudi Aramco's 400K bpd Jazan refinery remains offline until Aug 30 after Houthi attack. Ukraine struck Russian refineries overnight. Houthis attacked a cargo ship in Bab al-Mandib killing 3 crew (first commercial deaths). Hormuz shipping traffic fell to 6 vessels vs. 10-day average of 11. Polymarket assigns only 47% odds of traffic normalization by year-end.

bullets.title: NVDA mobilizes $500B AI infrastructure financing with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman, KKR
bullets.body: Nvidia confirmed partnerships with six major financial institutions to mobilize over $500B in third-party capital for AI compute financing platforms. NVDA co-invests up to 25% with third-party decision-making, limiting circular concerns; current direct credit exposure is only $3.5B in lease guarantees. Morgan Stanley reiterates OW with $288 PT, seeing potential 10%+ FY29 EPS upside from revenue-sharing annuity streams. Bears note the MOU is not binding and raises overbuild risk.

bullets.title: Intel prices $20B equity offering at $95/share with $100B+ demand—AI infrastructure capex surge driver
bullets.body: Intel upsized its secondary offering from $15B to $19.7B (210.5M shares at $95/share, a ~6.5% discount) on more than $100B of demand—its first public equity sale. Proceeds targeted for capex and working capital. The fundraise and elevated 2027 capex guidance signal confidence in sustained AI infrastructure demand, and analysts see it as supportive of Intel's advanced packaging and AI silicon positioning.

bullets.title: NFIB small business optimism hits 1-year high at 99.8; hiring plans jump record 9 points
bullets.body: July NFIB headline optimism rose to 99.8 vs. 97.4 prior, above consensus of 97.5. Hiring plans surged 9 points to 20%, the sharpest monthly jump on record excluding the Covid rebound. Capex plans jumped 5 points to 25%. Price increases fell 7 points and inflation as top concern dropped for the first time this year. Uncertainty ticked up and credit conditions tightened slightly.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex for 2026 exploded from $460B to $789B in six months; IG spreads near all-time wides
bullets.body: Hyperscaler 2026 capex projections rose 72% to $789B over six months. Goldman estimates US AI investment at nearly $600B (~2% GDP). Despite equities at all-time highs and VIX below 20, hyperscaler IG credit spreads blew out to 143 bps in August—up 43 bps from May-June lows—the widest in the dataset, an historically unprecedented combination. DayOne Data Centers confidentially filed for a $5B IPO.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure bifurcation: infrastructure software sees largest net buying; applications software remains unloved
bullets.body: Infrastructure software saw the largest net buying among tech subsectors over the past two weeks; MSFT RSI hit 79 and is trading at its widest premium to the 200-day MA since October. Semiconductor subsectors diverged post-earnings (GLW +18% vs TXN/NXPI -5%/-12%). Applications software faces significant short interest as the short side of the AI trade; HUBS, KVYO generating investor confusion. Enterprise AI inference costs fell to 2026 lows amid price wars and Chinese open-source competition.

bullets.title: Texas data center moratorium threatens grid-connected AI buildout; behind-meter plays accelerate
bullets.body: Texas Gov. Abbott called for a 40-60 day audit/quasi-moratorium on data center development, with risks that other states follow. NRG and VST are most exposed as IPPs. Behind-the-meter plays (BE, SEI) expected to accelerate in 2H26. ERCOT filed to delay Batch Zero process with six large loads expected in August QSA. Morgan Stanley notes $6B in collateral from large loads supports credibility of Batch Zero demand.

bullets.title: Fed's Hammack hawkish: inflation won't fall on its own; rates not meaningfully restricting
bullets.body: Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said she 'doesn't see inflation coming back down on its own,' that the current rate is 'not meaningfully restricting the economy,' and that she would 'probably need some number of rate hikes.' Markets are pricing ~52% probability of a 25bp hike in September per pre-market data. UBS economists expect the FOMC to hold at 3.75% through year-end, while fed funds futures imply ~125 bps of cumulative tightening by December.

bullets.title: Berkshire returns to net equity buyer; SPX P/S ratio at historic extremes
bullets.body: Berkshire Hathaway bought $23.47B and sold $3.69B of equities in Q2 2026, ending 14 consecutive quarters as a net seller. Meanwhile, PLTR trades at 72x TTM P/S vs. NVDA at 21x and S&P 500 at 3.5x. Bitcoin ETFs saw $850M+ weekly inflows, the largest since April.

bullets.title: Wolfe: US deficits remain near 6% GDP through FY27; AI productivity alone can't fix federal debt
bullets.body: Wolfe DC Policy argues that even an optimistic 50bp AI productivity boost leaves the debt rising indefinitely. CBO assumes only 10bp annual productivity gain from AI. Treasury is already front-loading shorter-tenor issuance, signaling concern. Divided government in 2027 expected to produce policy stasis with no major fiscal shift before 2028.

bullets.title: China auto sales down 21.1% YoY in July; EV penetration hits 65.1% with exports surging
bullets.body: China sold 1.47M passenger cars in July, down 21.1% YoY. NEV retail penetration hit 65.1%. NEV exports surged +147.8% YoY to 540K units. Tesla domestic China retail was only ~27.2K units (-33% YoY/-48% MoM) despite wholesale of 93.6K (+38% YoY). ICE wholesale fell 24% YoY.

bullets.title: Energy sector up 34% YTD, outperforming S&P by 2,100bps; XLE technical setup bullish
bullets.body: Energy is 2026's top YTD sector with +34% gains, outperforming S&P 500 by 2,100bps and Tech by 1,200bps. XLE exhibits a High-and-Tight Flag technical pattern with a $73 target vs $60.18 close, trading above an upward-sloping 200-day MA with positive weekly and monthly momentum.

bullets.title: US-Iran stalemate: Wolfe sees $85 WTI manageable for consumers, $120+ needed to fully offset OBBB stimulus
bullets.body: Both the US and Iran are absorbing enough pain to want a pause but unclear who cracks first. US munitions stockpiles are severely depleted with four of seven key munitions over 50% expended. Iran's rial is down 50% since mid-2025 with core CPI near 50% YoY. At $85 WTI through year-end, consumer drag is $116B vs $188B OBBB stimulus—manageable. WTI averaging $120+ would be needed to fully offset OBBB stimulus.

bullets.title: Korean DRAM export prices rising; CXMT 17nm DDR5 yield exceeds 90%—memory upcycle intact but China competition looms
bullets.body: Korea's DRAM export unit prices trended higher in early August. DRAM exports $4.62B (+4% MoM, +32% QoQ). However, Chinese media report CXMT's 17nm DDR5 yield exceeded 90% with product now available in large volumes in spot markets, posing a medium-term competitive threat to SK Hynix and Samsung. UBS notes NVDA's lower HBM specs for Vera Rubin Ultra boost 2027 HBM consumption to 61.5B Gb from 58.7B Gb.

bullets.title: Regional banks KRE in 4-day losing streak with bearish divergence; private credit showing stress
bullets.body: KRE declined for four consecutive days, its longest losing streak since May, forming a bearish divergence pattern. Separately, quarterly reports from major private credit funds show worsening loan health and declining investor returns despite manager reassurances. IG Hyperscaler OAS spreads reached 143 bps in August—43 bps wider than May-June lows—while stocks traded at all-time highs, an historically unprecedented divergence.

bullets.title: Anthropic eyes September/October IPO at ~$965B valuation; $9.1B Riot compute deal signals frontier AI capex scale
bullets.body: Anthropic is meeting investors ahead of a potential IPO as early as September, per WSJ, targeting a ~$965B valuation per X sources. Polymarket assigns 66% probability by Oct 31. Anthropic simultaneously struck a $9.1B, 20-year cloud computing deal with Riot (191 MW, Rockdale TX) for frontier AI compute. OpenAI completed a $7B secondary share sale at $852B valuation.
